title: Household staff meals: should your chef cook them too?
meta_title: Household Staff Meals: What to Agree With Your Chef | myCHEF
meta_description: Should a full-time chef in Dubai cook for household staff as well as the family? Compare three arrangements and build a staff-meals brief that works.
excerpt: Three arrangements for staff meals alongside family cooking, with a brief checklist and a worked week.
body_html:
In many Dubai households the question comes up within the first week: should the chef who cooks for the family also prepare household staff meals for drivers, nannies and helpers? It can work well, but only as a deliberate arrangement with its own brief — not as an unspoken extra added to the family menu. This guide compares three common arrangements, lists what the brief should cover and shows a worked week. If you are setting up or reviewing a recurring arrangement, start with the full-time private chef service page.

Three arrangements and their trade-offs

ArrangementHow it worksSuits
One shared menuStaff eat the same dishes as the family, at their own timeSmall teams with no conflicting dietary needs
A parallel simpler dishThe chef cooks a second, simpler dish in the same sessionLarger teams, different mealtimes or preferences
Prep-only supportThe chef preps ingredients; staff cook their own foodStaff who prefer their own cooking and flexible hours

There is no default answer; the right choice depends on how many people eat, when, and how the household prefers to organise it.

What the brief should cover

  • Who eats staff meals, on which days, and at what times.
  • Whether portions match the family count or a separate headcount.
  • Dietary notes for staff, recorded with the same care as the family's.
  • Where staff eat and which dishes and cutlery they use.
  • Who washes up after staff meals, and when.
  • Whether the arrangement runs on the chef's working days only.

A worked week (hypothetical)

A household with two helpers and a driver chooses the parallel-dish arrangement. The family eats at 19:30; staff eat at 17:00 before the evening service. The chef cooks one simple hot dish for 17:00 — often something that uses the day's prep trim — then cooks the family menu. The helpers wash their own dishes; the chef washes what the cooking used. Total extra cooking time across the week stays modest, because the 17:00 dish was folded into the existing prep. The arrangement was written into the household brief rather than agreed by habit.

Reviewing the arrangement

Staff arrangements change with rosters and seasons. A short review after the first month — using the same structure as a household menu review — keeps the arrangement from drifting. Note what changed, who it affects and what the chef needs to know for next week.

Next step: add staff meals as a line in your household brief and confirm the arrangement when you book the full-time private chef service. Related reading: writing a household menu brief and planning cover for the chef's day off.
